note: Both sets share the same core claims and both fabricate the note-1 quote "1. ALL CU" to assert a copper material, when the page actually says current-carrying cable is USE-2, 10 GA. Set A adds two misbound claims treating the symbol number "3" as a connection target for SA1-6 and SA1-7, plus an SA1-10 terminal-polarity claim whose quote ("+") does not bind the polarity to that module. Set B formulates the 11-labels more accurately as interconnecting component values between the SA1-6/SA1-7 and SA2-19/SA2-20 pairs, and avoids A's extra misbindings. Both sets are otherwise near-identical, with the same duplicated "value 3 / component value 3" pairs and the same vague treatment of the in-symbol "3".
remarks: Note 1 reads 'ALL CURRENT CARRYING CABLE IS USE-2, 10.G.A' but both sets quote it as '1. ALL CU' and derive a copper-material claim — a shared fabrication/garble worth fixing in the extractor. The in-symbol '3' (circle inside every module) and the '11' callouts at the four inter-module junctions are ambiguous symbols (legend/detail references rather than engineering values), yet both sets emit many 'value 3' claims and treat 11 as a connection endpoint; these should be classified as symbol references, not values. Important page facts (SUNPREME GX290 module, frameless glass design per E-502, #10G bonding jumper, USE-2 10 GA cable) are absent from the shown samples, though they may sit in the shared unshown claims.
